title: Loaner Term Limits and Due-Date Extension Allowances by Program
content:
For Courtesy Transportation Agreements, each program sets how long one agreement may run, how many times its due date may be extended, and whether an extension depends on the repair order still being open.

| Program | Most days one agreement may run, extensions included | Most due-date extensions | Extension only while the repair order is still open |
|---|---|---|---|
| Same-Day Courtesy Loaner | 1 | 0 | Yes |
| Courtesy Loaner - Compact | 7 | 2 | Yes |
| Courtesy Loaner - Midsize | 7 | 2 | Yes |
| Courtesy Loaner - SUV | 7 | 2 | Yes |
| Warranty Rental Loaner | 14 | 3 | Yes |
| Fleet Replacement Unit | 30 | 4 | No |

## What each column means

1. **Most days one agreement may run** is the maximum loaner days for the program, and it includes any extensions: extending a due date never lets an agreement run past this figure.
2. **Most due-date extensions** is the most times the due date of one agreement may be extended.
3. **Extension only while the repair order is still open** is a switch. Where it reads Yes, the due date is extended only while the repair order the loaner supports is still open. Where it reads No, as for the Fleet Replacement Unit, the program does not tie an extension to an open repair order.

## Points of judgement drawn from the table

- The Same-Day Courtesy Loaner shows 0 extensions, so the due date of a Same-Day agreement is never extended; its agreements also run at most 1 day.
- The Compact, Midsize and SUV programs share the same limits: 7 days and 2 extensions.
- The Warranty Rental Loaner allows the longest retail term, 14 days, with up to 3 extensions.
- The Fleet Replacement Unit allows up to 30 days and 4 extensions, and is the only program whose extensions are not conditioned on an open repair order.

## Hypothetical illustration

A Courtesy Loaner - Midsize agreement whose due date has already been extended twice has used the 2 extensions the program allows. A Warranty Rental Loaner agreement extended twice has used 2 of its 3. The extension counts in this illustration are invented for the example.
